sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Mehul Telecom is a Gujarat-focused handset retailer and bulk seller, not a telecom network operator or software platform. The attractive element is genuine reported revenue scaling with a low fixed-store-asset model; the decisive weakness is that the company continues to fund inventory and customer credit while cash realization lags earnings. This is an emerging regional retail growth thesis, not a proven compounder. At the dated secondary close of ₹132, the conditional base produces 16.47%, only modestly above the 15% equity hurdle. That is not an actionable return forecast: material stock-assurance uncertainty puts G2 on Hold, and BSE liquidity remains unverified. Final classification: Hold — unresolved. Clear independent inventory/receivable evidence and a complete tradability test could change the investment conclusion; a cheaper price alone cannot clear those gates.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Mehul buys third-party mobile phones/accessories and sells through company outlets, franchise outlets and bulk customers. The April 2026 prospectus describes 6 COCO and 74 FOFO stores. Under the franchise model the franchisee bears local rent/staff/operating responsibility, while Mehul retains stock against refundable security deposits, recognizes gross product sales and shares margin/commission. Daily retail remittance is described, but bulk credit changes the cash profile. In 9 M December 2025, phones contributed 98.63% of revenue; accessories 1.37%. COCO/bulk-channel reported revenue was ₹110.0864 cr(72.43%) and FOFO ₹41.9012 cr(27.57%). The largest customer alone contributed 18.43%. The disclosed footprint is Gujarat; Rajkot 65.26% and Morbi 17.10% of 9 M sales create local concentration. Mobile Daddy generated only ₹0.0827 cr FY26 sales and does not establish a monetized technology platform. Manufacturer warranty/consumer-liability exposure and merchant financing fees remain operating costs. Franchise expansion shifts outlet fixed costs, not all inventory/credit risk, to partners.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: A local distribution network can reduce acquisition and store-opening effort, but brand resale is not brand ownership. No exclusive manufacturer territory, durable price premium or proprietary customer switching-cost evidence was established.9M top 10 suppliers provided 49.57% of purchases, largest 8.70%; those are supplier entities, not a manufacturer-brand split. The top 10 franchisees supplied 56.37% of franchise sales. Online discounting, direct brand stores and other regional chains constrain economics. Economic peers are Fonebox Retail, Jay Jalaram Technologies and Bhatia Communications & Retail; Mehul Colours is not a peer. The prospectus FY25 peer KPI table shows EBITDA margins 2.16%,2.11% and 4.94% respectively versus Mehul's 6.63% proforma FY25 and 6.82% operating FY26. This is not a current valuation comparison: peer year, scope and lease/channel mix differ, and Jay Jalaram's consolidated ₹667.68 cr sales must not be mixed with the ₹339.09 cr standalone valuation-table denominator. A superior reported margin is a question to verify, not automatic moat evidence.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Runway is conditional on selling and collecting profitable additional handset inventory, not simply signing more franchisees. Existing regional access makes a fading growth path plausible, but no verified store cohort proves the stock/cash required per opening. The base grows revenue 25/18/15/12/10/10% from FY26 into FY32, assumes 6.5% EBITDA,60 inventory days,31 receivable days and 30 payable days, plus supplier/government balances and franchise funding. Growth capex 0.3% of sales is separate from working capital and rent; franchised stock is not omitted. Two within-perimeter incremental-capital bridges are provided rather than a false ratio across the transfer. FY25→26 normalized incremental NOPAT ₹4.4369 cr divided by incremental operating IC ₹15.8874 cr is 27.93%, declining to 23.46% without extra franchise deposits. Predecessor FY23→24 also shows positive incremental economics under advance-classification bounds, but negative net capital in one stripped case makes level ROICNM. A 14–18% analytical capital-cost range does not by itself prove durable economic profit. CAP 6 recognizes demonstrated accounting reinvestment economics while CASH 2 prevents a high growth-quality designation; GQS is capped 5. As a deliberately approximate bottom-up cross-check, FY26 revenue divided by the 80 disclosed network units is ₹2.5015 cr per unit-equivalent. The base terminal annual revenue≈₹441 cr is 2.20×FY26: at unchanged throughput it needs≈176 network-unit equivalents;25% higher productivity reduces this to≈141, and 25% lower productivity raises it to≈235. These are not forecasts of physical store count or verified mature-store productivity because bulk sales dominate the company-operated channel and FY26 channel mix is not separately reliable. A roughly 2.2×network/productivity requirement therefore remains a hypothesis that must be accompanied by funded inventory/receivables, continued franchise deposits and the modeled 0.3% of sales capex. Actual store cohorts or disclosed bulk-customer throughput must replace this approximate scaling test before a high-confidence runway claim.

sections.text:
FY26 revenue ₹200.1201 cr less COGS ₹179.4047 cr gives gross profit ₹20.7154 cr. Operating EBITDA ₹13.6445 cr, EBIT ₹13.5871 cr and statutory PAT ₹9.9639 cr exclude only ₹0.0881 cr other income when computing operating profit. Gross purchases ₹203.6210 cr less allowances ₹12.2928 cr yield net purchases ₹191.3282 cr; a material rebate reduction could erode earnings rapidly. Commission ₹2.6989 cr and merchant fees ₹1.4546 cr are recurring, not exceptional add-backs. FY25 statutory PAT ₹5.8184 cr becomes ₹5.7362 cr in prospectus restatement because ₹0.0822 cr gratuity was recognized. The ₹0.70 cr higher government balance and tax provision in the prospectus exactly offset, a gross/net tax presentation difference rather than an asset hole. FY26 lacks a clear gratuity rollforward, so an analytical ₹0.038 cr recurring annual charge and ₹0.1107 cr obligation reserve are explicit, not alleged statutory corrections.

FY26 CFO starts with PAT 9.9639+DA 0.0574+tax 3.4313+finance 0.2801=13.7327(subject to ₹0.0001 rounding), then inventory−11.9235, debtors−10.4931, advances−1.8249, prepaid IPO−0.3265, noncurrent deposits−0.1401, payables+4.5027, current liabilities+1.5125, refundable deposits+3.0273 and provisions+0.0220; tax paid 1.8019 gives CFO−3.7130. For a more complete operating classification, add back the ₹0.3265 cr increase in prepaid IPO expenses to reported CFO: operating CFO before that financing-object outflow is−3.3865, and excluding refundable-deposit financing as well gives−6.4138. This favorable adjustment does not restore positive cash conversion; the deposit-only−6.7403 figure is not mislabeled fully normalized CFO. These deposits are repayable financing even when classified in statutory operating cash. FY25 cash flow includes transfer/start-up presentation and noncash share consideration; a single all-years ratio is not defensible. Same-perimeter ratios of sums are shown and explicitly qualified.

Inventory ₹30.1488 cr and receivables ₹17.0813 cr dominate assets.₹4.7185 cr debtors exceed six months(27.62%), including ₹1.7254 cr older than one year, with no allowance disclosed. Physical cash ₹2.69 cr is 98.19% of total cash ₹2.7397 cr; this is a verification sensitivity, not automatic confiscation. Gross debt ₹3.4636 cr includes ₹2.6743 cr term debt, ₹0.7615 cr 12-month business loan and ₹0.0278 cr director demand balance. Current term maturity ₹0.0955 cr is included once. sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹132 and 10,451,600 shares, market cap is ₹137.9611 cr. FY26 post-IPO-share EPS ₹9.53 implies 13.85×reported PE; normalized recurring-gratuity EPS is slightly lower. A naive March cash EV would combine a post-IPO share count with pre-IPO cash and is not presented as current EV. The dated cash reconstruction separates free cash from ₹22.95 cr IPO working-capital earmarks, remaining fees net of ₹0.399 cr already prepaid, and September legacy tax/claims. The base cutoff free cash ₹7.69 cr and restricted ₹18.55 cr are model outputs, not verified interim accounts. Signed entry surplus after reserve is used; deficits are never clipped into fictitious zero obligations. Earmarks fund only eligible current WC, not franchise refunds or debt repayment.

Scenarios retain cash until 20 October 2031, no dividends. Base exit 8×annual operating EBITDA, bear 5×, bull 10×; no extra property value is added to business EV. Terminal cash is reduced by operating floor and a 25% franchise-refund buffer, with residual debt deducted once. No-rescue conditional returns: bear NS(unfunded), base 16.47%, bull 30.95%. Bear mechanical terminal ₹55.01 and return-16.06% are explicitly unfinanceable arithmetic, not a supported expected return. Base terminal ₹282.86; bull ₹508.16. All ordinary investment returns remain NS under G2 Hold. Conditional base entry prices meeting 12/15/18% hurdles are ₹160.51/₹140.64/₹123.65, not unconditional buy levels. Funded reverse brackets imply about 10.20%/13.99%/17.65% uniform revenue growth respectively at unchanged 6.5% margin and 8×multiple. Solver reports finite funded brackets and residuals, not a boundary disguised as a solution.

Cash funding is tested from 31 March 2026, before IPO and before investment entry, through every monthly/stub interval and terminal reserve. Base cash floor is 0.75% of salesrun-rate(about 2.7 sales days), with 0.5–2% tests; this is an assumption, not a disclosed bank covenant. Future operating profit cannot finance the interval's upfront WC/capex/principal. Current-period interest/tax are assumed paid after receipts, with a full-prefunding sensitivity. No new bank facility or refinancing is assumed. Hypothetical rescue uses whole shares issued before each gap,25% discount and 5% fees, and reports gross/net/dilution. Any pre-entry rescue is a historical counterfactual, not something a present investor can arrange to repair the past; observed current shares remain unchanged. DCF is only a cash-flow crosscheck at an independently stated 18% discount rate, with 15/18/21% sensitivities and consistent cash reserves; it is not a reliable standalone point valuation under the stock-assurance hold. Two-way inventory×receivable and capex×deposit funding grids link operations to cash, alongside margin×multiple and discount×multiple grids. Execution cost 1/3/5% tests do not substitute for missing BSE liquidity.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest countercase is that apparent high-margin scale was bought with slow-moving handset inventory, bulk credit and refundable franchise funding. Loss of brand discounts, handset obsolescence and slower customer collections can happen together. The bear model lowers growth and margin while extending stock/debtor days and reducing supplier/franchise funding. It generates a maximum unfunded prefunding gap ₹7.53 cr, first appearing in the pre-entry historical reconstruction. That does not prove an actual historical default: it shows the adverse path cannot be funded under the declared timing and no-rescue assumptions. Its conditional IRR isnull even if later cash recovers. The hypothetical recapitalized path is separate and dilutes holders; it cannot validate the original share-count path. Creditors, supplier settlements and franchise refunds can consume cash before ordinary shareholders recover value. The permanent-loss risk is High, not simply volatility. A 5% inventory impairment requires ₹1.51 cr replacement/recognition, and 25% loss on debtors ₹4.27 cr; tests distinguish gross economic loss from additional collection delay. The thesis-break variables are independently confirmed stock quality, collection beyond six months and sustained cash conversion excluding refundable deposits. Lack of a proven moat means a lower multiple alone cannot protect against disappearing profits.

sections.text: A fivefold share price over five years requires 37.97% annualized return; tenfold requires 58.49%. From ₹132, targets are ₹660/₹1320 and equityvalues ₹689.81 cr/₹1379.61 cr before further issuance. At 8×exit EBITDA and roughly ₹66 cr net excess cash in the base, a 5×outcome needs about ₹78 cr EBITDA, or roughly ₹1200 cr revenue at 6.5% margin. 10×requires approximately ₹164 cr EBITDA and ₹2500 cr revenue. These are illustrative scale equations, not forecasts: required cash balances and dilution would change with that growth. The base ends around ₹441 cr annual revenue run-rate and 2.14×share value; even the bull is about 3.85×. Therefore neither 5×nor 10×is a supported central thesis. More stores and a large handset market do not remove the need to fund inventory, maintain brand economics and grow earnings per diluted share. A full high-growth rescue model would need independent operating evidence before making such a claim.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: 1. Obtain independent quantity, ownership and NRV evidence for ₹30.1488 cr Marchstock, including franchise locations; unresolved alternative audit assurance keeps G2 Hold. 2. Track collections of ₹4.7185 cr debtors older than six months and ₹1.7254 cr older than one year; worsening age mix or noncollection is a thesis-break signal, not merely a lower score. 3. Require rolling CFO/PAT≥0.8 and positive cash aftercapex, excluding refundable-deposit inflows, before upgrading CASH materially; one half-year alone is insufficient. 4. Reconcile IPO gross 27.73008, totalfees 2.7730, prepaid 0.3990 and ₹22.95 cr earmark to audited utilization and eligible working capital. 5. Track inventory 60 days/receivables 31 days/payables 30 days base targets and sensitivities; simultaneous inventory≥75/debtors≥45 days triggers a fresh funding review. 6. Test actual availability of cash, rather than accepting ₹2.69 cr physicalcurrency as equivalent to audited bank confirmations. 7. Monitor purchase allowances, gross margin and operating EBITDA; sustained marginbelow 5% materially weakens the valuation. 8. Require store count openings/closures and same-store sales without confusing network stock with additions; explain FY25 channel discrepancy. 9. Confirm debt repayments, franchise refund terms and gratuity rollforward, including no doublecounted current maturities. 10. Authenticate BSE 60 session mean/median, spread/circuits and current restrictions; rerun lot-rounded 2/5/10% exit tests. These are review triggers, not automatic orders or a promise of future surveillance.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved, with no new-purchase recommendation. BQS 5.16 and capped GQS 5.00 describe a growing but cash-intensive regional retailer, not a high-quality compounder. IAS NS is driven by a material financial-reliability hold and incomplete tradability/return evidence, not a hidden neutral valuation score. All quality, growth-quality and investment ranking flags arefalse until G2 is cleared; a complete score alone does not make a company ranking-eligible. G1/G3 are Conditional, not failures, because disclosed facts do not prove misconduct or actual insolvency. The conditional base at ₹132 offers only a modest spread over 15% and depends on maintaining 6.5% EBITDA and improving cash realization. A lower price affects P/R, not BQS; it cannot authenticate stock or create exit liquidity. Revisit only after independent stock/receivable confirmation, a reliable IPO usage/cash bridge and BSE liquidity record. Existing holders face different execution constraints from new buyers; no position size or personal suitability is assumed.

sections.text:
Primary sources are the FY26 annual report with full main/CARO/IFC audit, the final April 2026 prospectus with restated company and predecessor statements, and the FY26 audited result filing. Source hashes and exact locators are retained for rechecking. The dated security master verifies identity/lot/share count but does not prove current BSE restrictions. The ₹132 quote is a retained historical broker row and stays secondary. Octoberstore announcements and the price clarification are not promoted from snippets to verified claims where the original BSE attachment was inaccessible. 5/10 year CAGR s, handset units/ASP, mature-store cohorts, manufacturer-brand concentration, detailed rebate contracts, independent stock confirmations and complete BSE turnover/spread data remain ND. Neither missing data nor an allegation is silently scored as fact.

Definitions: operating EBITDA=PBT+finance+DA−otherincome; normalized FY25 profit uses prospectusgratuity; FY26 recurringgratuity is a separate analytical allowance. Average-day ratios use consistent average opening/closing balances and purchases for payabledays; transfer-year averages are NM. Cash C Fs retain original classifications and supply economic deposit-adjusted measures separately. Capital bridges exclude cash, IPO prepaids and identified nonoperating investments, with unclassified predecessor advances bounded. Model tax 25%, run-rate/interpolation, cash floor, margins, growth, WC days, capex and exitmultiples are assumptions, not management forecasts. No original document reproductions or personal identifiers are embedded in the reusable package; retained financial observations reproduce calculations, not a fresh authentication of omitted originals. The decisive open question is whether reported stock and collectible receivables will become owner cash without persistent new external financing.

summary: Mehul Telecom is a Gujarat-focused handset retailer and bulk seller, not a telecom network operator or software platform. The attractive element is genuine reported revenue scaling with a low fixed-store-asset model; the decisive weakness is that the company continues to fund inventory and customer credit while cash realization lags earnings. This is an emerging regional retail growth thesis, not a proven compounder. At the dated secondary close of ₹132, the conditional base produces 16.47%, only modestly above the 15% equity hurdle. That is not an actionable return forecast: material stock-assurance uncertainty puts G2 on Hold, and BSE liquidity remains unverified. Final classification: Hold — unresolved. Clear independent inventory/receivable evidence and a complete tradability test could change the investment conclusion; a cheaper price alone cannot clear those gates.
